review_highlights.comment: I love Prof Matlock and learned so much in this class! But I definitely found it very intellectually challenging. I feel like I really did have to work to earn my grade. I loved getting his feedback, he took the time and was very insightful. The class is also very approachable for non-classics majors such as myself.

One of the few people that I have learned something from. If you like a seminar-based class that is full of philosophical discussions and insights, this is the one for you. Although his lectures can be long, please pay attention to what is being taught...it might come in handy, especially if you didn't really read an assigned homework book.

Dr. Matlock is an amazing lecturer and I really loved his class!!! He's super personable however beware there is SO MUCH READING and if you don't do it you will feel lost. However I didn't read most of it and was still able to get A's on the paper, he is an easy grader and great guy so absolutely take his class if you like to read.

Easily one of the best professors I've ever had! Like any Classics course, there's a lot of reading, but Dr. Matlock divides it up really well and explains it more thoroughly in class. He's super understanding, and wants you to do well and like the course! He gives good feedback on assignments and is accessible for more help outside of class.

He makes this class quite interesting and really understands and cares about what he's teaching and how he does it. There are reading quizzes about every other week however doesn't grade hard as long as you show you have an understanding of what is going on. There is a lot of reading, but it is doable. I would recommend taking him.

analysis.name: Prince Allotey
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Statistics is not an easy course, but Prince makes complex concepts understandable. He is kind, friendly, and cares about his students' success. Attendance is not required, but I highly recommend attending every lecture because he shares valuable insights for tests and assignments. His lectures are engaging, and he allows cheat sheets on tests.

Professor Allotey was always super nice, but I would say this is just a bad class in general. Yes the lowest test is dropped, but after the first exam most the questions are write in. I had a tutor for our tests and still performed poorly. The class itself is also just pretty boring, he has an accent which sometimes makes it hard to understand him

It separates the boys from the men and the girls from the women. I feel like I barely learned anything throughout the course, but the weight of homework and labs saved my grade. He also drops 1 test grade, 1 homework and 2 labs, so that also helps a lot. You can use a cheat sheet on every test. I passed, but I wouldn't say I know much about stats

I think, out of all the stats professors, he was good, just very lecture-heavy. The labs seem kinda pointless, but basically cushion grades. You have weekly homework, but it's super helpful if you actually do them yourself (not chat), and the tests are very similar to them (sometimes literally the same questions). study w/ the hw and test reviews!

Allotey is the only reason I passed STAT2000. I am so bad at math, but he saw I always gave it my best effort and helped where he could. If you show up to lectures (even though they're not required) you might get some points at the end of the semester! He truly cares if you pass or not, especially if it's a required credit for your major.

review_highlights.comment: Best professor for Gen Chem! There is extra credit for going to recitation and so much practice problems that prepare great for the tests. She does pre class videos that go over the topic for that week, so the subject is not completely new in class, which definitely helped me understand the topic more and i feel like is better than reading checks

She is so sweet and really knows chemistry! She is great at lecturing, and I think she truly is the best professor to have to get thru a course as difficult as this one... just get ready to study a lot (she offers tons of resources!!) and PREPARE for the exams... hard content AND difficult word problems :') Also, the lab was really manageable!

Dr. A is by far the best professor I have had at UGA. Her lectures and practice problems are incredibly helpful for the exams. She is super accessible outside class and truly cares about her students' success. I got a D on the first exam, had a meeting with her, and finished the class with an A+. Put in the extra studying and it will all pay off.

I loved Dr. A! She provided us with so many resources to prepare us for exams so make sure to do all of them to do well. Although chem 2 was very dense and difficult to understand, going to her office hours and asking her questions helped out a lot. Her lectures might be a little boring but she goes through practice problems so it's worth it.

Loved her so much for 1311H, my issues with her are in 1312H. The extra practice posted is not reflective of the long (and very wordy) exams. Not sure what's going on this semester, but the exams are so hard. She's is still the best instructor for this class, but be ready for 1312H to be harder than 1311H.

You don't need to have any music experience (I didn't) or even be good at playing the drums (I'm still bad). He is very chill and understanding, and his lectures are interesting. If you need an easy arts credit, take this class. You just need to go to class and play some drums. You don't need to have any music experience (I didn't) or even be good at playing the drums (I'm still bad). It's only graded by attendance, and he gives you 3 free absences. He is very chill and understanding, and his lectures are interesting.

Most fun and chill class ever. Trained musicians and people who have never seen music before can all enjoy this class because it's so hands on and Nico is the best! I genuinely learned about so many different cultures and instruments. Show up to class and hit the drum and you have an A.

Nico's class was super chill, stress free, and fun to participate in. All you gotta do is show up, log your attendance, hit some drums, and don't be doom scrolling on your phone. If you need a class that fulfills your multicultural credit and you don't wanna be writing essays or reports take this course.

Literally easiest class ever, just show up and play drums. No musical experience necessary, and hes really funny too and trys to engage the class. Only graded on attendance, you get 3 unexcused absences too.

Dr Heil is great, I would really recommend taking this course. He really cares about the material, and it shows during his lectures. I am not even in the marine bio field, but I thoroughly enjoyed this class and would take it again in a heartbeat. Tests are not too hard if you study, hw load is very manageable. One of the best professors at UGA.

Dr. Heil is absolutely INCREDIBLE. I would highly, highly recommend taking this class. The course load is super manageable, as well. Also, if you need a lab with it, I would recommend applying to do the weekend at Skidaway. It is only 2 days and fulfills your entire lab credit for the course, as well as an hour of credit. & it is super fun!!!!

He is the best professor I've ever had. Love this guy. He's so sweet and really cares about his class. You can tell the absolute passion he has for the marine environment just by the way he teaches and tells stories. analysis.name: Allison Howard
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 82 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: ADORE Dr Howard. She is genuinely the coolest! This course was harder than any of my other psych classes at UGA so definitely be prepared to study for exams, but she is an incredible professor, so I still highly recommend the class. Tests are a mix of MC, matching, and free response. She has participation grades sporadically, so go to class.

I would take her class again and again. It is so well organized, and she genuinely cares about her students. The topic in itself was also very interesting to me. I always studied the night before and did very well on all her exams. You can also drop the final. If you're looking for a good psyc class to fill a requirement, this is the one.

I will genuinely miss Dr. Howard and her class. It was very interesting especially when the class participates. Exams were completely fair; study flashcards and definitions, and HW she gives (which is weekly, and reasonable, and helpful). Has one book that you read, it was really good! One assignment on it, which was a zoom. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!!

TAKE HER! She was very kind and cared about the topics. She made it interesting and didn't give a lot of homework. Her lectures directly related to the test material and the tests were super easy, mainly just knowing vocab. Also the final is optional since you can drop one test and its online so if you have to take it, its not bad.

She is very interesting. The slides get posted and there are tophat questions that pop up randomly during class throughout the semester for attendance, but can answer from home so attendance is somewhat mandatory. The 3 tests make up most of your grade and the final can be exempted as 1 test gets dropped. Homework is basically unlimited attempts.

Prof Miller is great. I've taken him twice now. He's very understanding when approached with issues and reaches out because he actually cares about his students. His style of teaching also keeps class interesting when the material can be boring at times. Take this professor.

Andrew is such a nice person and is very understanding. However, this class felt a little bit disorganized and we were expected to learn a lot of niche concepts/people. Also, his grading is very confusing and you will never know where you stand.

Andrew as a person is fine but he is a very interesting teacher. He focuses on the most niche parts of history. He also has a podcast assignment that he grades as if you are a professional script writer.

analysis.name: Renny Badra
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I had a great experience with Dr. Badra. It was a flipped classroom which i dont do well with, but as long as you put in the effort you should be fine. He is well organized and accessible outside of class whenever needed. Exams were very tough and harsh grading. I'd say go to office hours whenever possible and use the textbook to your advantage.

He's an amazing teacher with an extremely well-designed eLC. The flipped class format actually works well if you put in the effort and work. Tests are brutal and grading is harsh, but circuits is naturally a hard class. I strongly recommend him because you will definitely learn a lot. He's very forgiving with assignment deadlines and is flexible.

Badra is the most “nothing to write home about” kind of professor you can get, and that is honestly a good thing. Lectures are mundane, labs are very manageable, and plenty of time to do them. His eLC is well organized with lots of resources. There's no curving on assessments, but we get a cheat sheet, so. He's a nice dude with a good intro course.

Badra is very kind, but his class is very difficult. Although at first it does not seem like a lot, the semester catches up to you. The class is flipped and has pre-lecture quizzes twice a week, weekly in-class quizzes, weekly labs, long homeworks, and a difficult midterm and final. He does not give much partial credit on his very difficult exams.

Dr. Badra is a great professor, but his class is challenging. His lectures, pre-quizzes, home assignments, and quizzes are helpful for learning the material and keep you on track in the course. He is very helpful in the lab as well if you are struggling. His tests are very difficult but fair, and they are not worth a lot of the total course grade.

analysis.name: Bethany Chapman

review_highlights.comment: MEMORIZE THE ASSERTIONS! If you pay attention in class she literally tells you exactly what to write for the FRQ on exams. Quizzes aren't that bad and she gives bonus questions as well as curves exams. I learned a lot and i was genuinely engaged in her lectures. Do the HW problems even though they're optional: they make up a lot of quiz questions.

Showing up to mandatory lecture was exhausting. The lectures are full of information, and Chapman talks at light speed, so good luck taking notes. Incredibly picky on FRQ on test ("only wants a couple sentences", but actually expected paragraphs). Pretty much no extra credit. Does curve tests which was nice. Good luck.

Real issue with her is that she is an extreme nitpicker and will take off points for things that are ridiculous. The written response has to be worded exactly the way she wants or you get points off even if you said the exact same thing worded differently. She should have practice written responses with feedback before the exam in that case.

The class is doable but read the textbook so you understand things conceptually better (95% of the course is understanding and memorizing concepts). I got a B+ only from studying the night before for every test. She also curved the last two tests. Could have made an A with actual studying

Professor Chapman's Systems class was more challenging than it needed to be. The tests were fine. The online projects were frustrating because she did not teach you how to do many of the things that you will be required to use. I personally thought she was not very helpful when I asked her questions about the material. Maybe try another professor.

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had! The difficultly if for just precal in general, not him specifically!  PLEASE TAKE HIM!!!!!

I would never have expected a class on teaching K-5 math to be so hard, but he spends his time to carefully break things down so that its easy to see how to explain things at multiple grade levels, and I love that he takes time to build an inclusive and warm classroom. Tests are similar to the in-class activities and homework, so it's overall easy.

Truly awesome professor. He really cares about his students, not just doing well in class but in general. 4 tests 10 quizzes and ~2 hw webassigns weekly. Tests are very fair- if you listen to lectures u shouldn't have to study much- and quizzes are easy. Pretty much everything on them is on the homework. Super nice guy and wonderful teacher!

Those who haven't taken calculus before, please go to his office hours if you're struggling even a tiny bit. He let me makeup 3 quizzes when I gave up temporarily and didn't go to class for 3 weeks. Lectures hard to understand for first-timers but he is one of the nicest teachers ever, and will try to help you out as best he can.

He is the best professor I have taken at UGA!! All he wants is for his students to succeed and will do everything he can to help you. Very helpful in office hours and will even set up a zoom if you are confused on something while studying. Also gives so much partial credit on exams. TAKE HIM!!!

analysis.name: Brent Shuman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I loveee this class! The content is super interesting and Dr. Shuman is very nice. There are exams every other week but it's actually way better than 4 big exams because the volume of content on each exam is way less and the whole system is way less stressful. I would totally recommend Dr. Shuman and the honors sections of this class!

Dr. Shuman is great! Knows his stuff but his slides can be confusing and a little disorganized. If you take notes and use the resources he provides tho, you'll be fine. Exams every 2 weeks, but loved it cause they had less content, lots of bonus questions, and mostly MC. Seriously, such a manageable course! Heads up, he is a pretty slow grader...

I honestly loved Shuman. Everyone talks about Lemon, but i would highly recommend him. I found the course load manageable, the tests fair (although sometimes a little unclearly written), and his lectures engaging. He is a funny and nice, a young prof. The recitations prepare you well for his exams, which there were 5. I would take him again!

Dr. Shuman goes through the slides very quickly, which can make it hard to follow the content at times. There will be some units that are inherently easier than others, and there is a lot of extra credit at the end of the semester! Complete all of the given recitation and textbook problems, and fill in the learning objectives to get an A.

I was really scared to take Shuman because so many people say that you're going to fail if you don't take Lemon, but I was pleasantly surprised! He's pretty approachable and willing to work with your schedule if you need to take the test on another date or something. Tests are definitely difficult but he's pretty fair about grading.

analysis.name: Audrey Haynes
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 453 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: If you take her online then good news: everything is open book/note! Yes, some of the questions can be difficult, but if you read the chapter and did the study guide you're pretty much set. The only videos you are REQUIRED to watch are a few that you have quizzes on. Lectures are optional, or if you just want to skim the slides she has that too.

Professor Haynes was the best professor I've had here so far. She doesn't just want you to pass her tests, she wants you to learn the material and really apply it. She's even inspired me to minor in Political Science. You will have to read the book, but the info is relevant so it isn't terrible. Online quizzes every week can be a grade booster too.

Dr. Haynes is very approachable/understanding if you ever need to speak with her. The textbook is very dense so ATTEND LECTURE because her powerpoints break up a lot of the info you need to know. Tests are not easy but quite fair if you go over the readings/activities she assigns. Breakouts are pointless but mandatory. Overall a good experience :)

I enjoyed taking Dr. Haynes's class online! Her assignments require a lot of critical thinking, and if you're ever stuck or need feedback on an assignment, she's more than happy to help you. Her assignments aren't hard, but make sure not to fall behind! Also, she offers a good amount of extra credit if you ever need a little boost!

Dr. Haynes is hands down one of the best professors at UGA. If I had the chance I would take every class she offered. She is one of the most caring and involved professors I have ever had and I highly recommend taking any of her classes. Attendance is required but you will want to be there.

review_highlights.comment: This was a great class! Dr. Burke is incredibly kind and made this class fun. The work was very easy and the tests were all multiple choice. Attendence is measured and graded using Tophat. She's a very nice person and grades fairly too. If you have any issues, she will definitely work with you.

Love this teachers enthusiasm! Love this course because of her passion for the subject. Lots of group work (assignments are done in class and turned in as you leave). She encourages field work and extra credit opportunities reflect this. Peer review article project with many submissions, not hard though.

Dr. Burke is extremely caring and her lectures are very interesting. Attendance is recorded and there are tophat questions, but the class is very easy and lectures are great. It feels like I'm seeing a nature documentary most of the time. Some group projects and lots of extra credit.

Dr. Burke is one of the sweetest professors you'll ever meet. She literally said at the beginning of class that she understands this class is mostly for nonscience majors, so she won't grade harshly. She stuck to her word. Attendance is mandatory, but you only have to attend 80% of classes to get an A in attendance. Definitely take this class!!!!

analysis.name: Barbara McCord
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Dr. McCord can seem a little strange at first, but her class is easy and she is very accessible. Attendance is not necessary to do well in the class. She has 3-4 in-class work days that are required for credit. She assigns online homework and does examples in class. She posts previous exams and sometimes lets you rework tests for 1/2 credit.

She's a little bit disorganized and the lectures don't really help much. The class problems and old tests help for the exams. Attendance is only mandatory on class problem days. She takes forever to grade everything, I got Bs on all the midterms and never got my final back but I got an A in the class pretty easily.

It is a flipped classroom, but you don't need to watch the videos if you go to class. To be honest, she is not the best teacher, but is very nice and teaches the easiest fluids class. You are allowed to bring one cheat sheet, front and back for each test. Also, the TAs host study sessions before each test that are SUPER helpful.

I stopped going to class at some point during the semester, but it's very much passable if you just watch the pre-class videos and do all the review materials. Exam review sessions hosted by the TA's are really helpful. This is a flipped class, so in class, she only works problems. She's a bit unorganized but nice.

If you go to class, read the textbook, and work the homework problems, you'll be fine. If you skip class, you won't do that well. She is always willing to help you understand material and is very approachable. Just don't be lazy like the person below and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Jack Bass
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: I'm not going to say he's the best professor, but I feel like a lot of these reviews are being overly critical. His lectures were boring, but you just got to pay attention and read the textbook. My main critique is the harsh grading of the labs by TAs, one line of inconsistent indention will get you an 85% even if everything else was perfect.

His lectures were BAD. He was nice, but if you do not have prior knowledge, you are better taking one of the other professors. His exams were on paper, and difficult. This class was so much harder than 1302 and I think it was entirely because I had Brad Barnes for 1302. Quizzes were insanely difficult as well. Labs were okay.

Professor Bass is a really young guy, and is extremely knowledgeable and caring. Breath of fresh air for UGA CS department.

I attended very class, made a 100 on every homework assignment, went to tutoring regularly, and still failed every test. Good luck.

Professor Bhan's lectures are interesting and engaging and she's really funny in a nerdy accounting sense. She is very available after class and with her office hours. Lecture heavy, no homework, pop quizzes are easy if you pay attention, but attendance is pretty much mandatory with a few drops. review_highlights.comment: Dr. Little is an incredible professor. She does not follow the syllabus, so be prepared to adjust. Her best classes are ones where she improvises. The tests and quizzes are online and she was always very understanding. The syllabus said attendance mandatory but you would never get penalized for missing! 10/10 would take again.

Exams are open-note and there aren't many assignments. She cares more about discussing the material than memorizing it! Dr. Byers was my fav professor my first semester here. Ecology on Campus was so fun and such a break from my difficult schedule. INCOMING FRESHMAN TAKE THIS FYOS!!!

analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 314 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I can honestly not say enough good things about Dr. Drake. By far the best teacher I have ever had. He makes you remember the importance of learning for its own sake and he genuinely cares about the topics in history. I never thought I would actually enjoy a 9 am history class but I found myself in shock when it was time to leave. He's awesome.

Professor Drake is fine himself, but the material is extremely heavy. The only grades in the class are for 3 essay based tests and final 10-page essay worth 50% of your grade. There is really no rubric for any test or exam and they could literally be over anything. You go into the tests having no idea what the one question he'll ask will be about.

Tests formats are all the same, including the final. There are two sections, ID terms and short answer. In total, five "questions". You have to write everything you know about a single name, word, or quote. And based off of your clarity and ability to relate the term/quote back to a bigger picture determines your grade in the class.

Dr. Drake was very engaging and made learning history fun! The tests (which were all essays) were doable/flexible, especially since you can pick and choose what you write about. There are pop quizzes throughout the semester (between 5-10 max), so beware of that. Overall, he is a great professor who teaches history in a way that sticks.

I loved Professor Drake. Extremely interesting lectures, always had some sort of personal anecdote and incorporated Athens into the lectures. However this class is extremely TA dependent and grading tends to be harsh. Taking good notes and reading the primary sources is critical in doing well. Pop quizzes every couple of weeks but not too bad

analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: People hate on the flipped classroom, respectfully so, BUT as long as you are intentional with the videos and take notes, you'll do fine. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you go, you get an extra attempt on the in-class quiz and worksheet, which makes a difference. She's one of the sweetest professors I've had yet.

She is so nice and she gives so many chances to do well. There is extra credit assignments for every unit, and you can retake any test during the final period. It is a flipped classroom so there is a good bit of outside classroom work, but her online lectures are easy to understand, if you take notes on them you will do well in this class

She means well and is a nice person but she is not a good professor. She overloads with the amount of work given and does not explain things in class very clearly and expects a lot of understanding just from watching an hour and a half worth of videos. Gives career work which isn't necessary and gives too many pre-class videos to watch with notes.

You can tell she cares a lot about the students and is trying. However, she tried a flipped classroom and it is pretty bad. So many videos and they are so boring and hard to learn from. The tests are not objective and they are a lot of trick questions without straight up answers. She means very well but the way the class is structured is not it.

She is very sweet and means well, but the flipped classroom has not worked super well. The lecture videos outside of class take tons of time, and the tests are VERY tricky. They are all application based so even if you have studied all of the material, it doesn't show. The graphing worksheets in class are very frustrating and not helpful.

analysis.name: Alexander Spektor
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Spektor is always willing to help you out. He's a little intimidating and expects a lot out of you, but he really cares about his students.

Very smart guy and able to look at Russian literature in a lense that was very eye opening to me. The class made me like reading again. Do be a little weary as you are reading 2000 pages worth of books, so you gotta be ready to read and then write good essays on them, but if you can do that, truly one of the most rewarding classes at UGA

Do not take this class unless you are ACTUALLY interested in Russian History. Be prepared to have more homework for this class than any other class you've taken. Should have been a simple class but turned out to be much more than I thought. He is an easy and generous grader but you have pop quizzes EVERYDAY based on readings/films.

Spektor gives great lectures. Discussions are elaborate and many topics are explored. He will answer any questions and is always open to help. His passion of teaching is very clear along with a good sense of humor. He takes the class seriously along with making sure that every student is good. I recommend any of his classes completely.

Sasha has been my favorite teacher at UGA. He is an entertaining professor who is beyond passionate about his subject. The man is very intelligent and got his PhD from Harvard. The 2050 course covered very interesting and complex material, but was graded on the easy side.

review_highlights.comment: This is my second time taking one of Dr. Sperling's courses. If you're an INTL major I definitely recommend taking his classes. Great guy, awesome Proffessor.

Sperling is one of the most intellectual and qualified professors I have ever had at UGA. He knows so much about the field and teaches in a fair and neutral POV (which is very hard to do for this class topic). He ensures everyone remains respectful during discussions. The group projects seem bad, but they truly help your understanding

Dr. Sperling provides a welcoming atmosphere for educated opinions and discussions on difficult topics. He practically never shares her personal opinion, and creates a class meant to educate rather than memorize or have busy work. Loved the class and I'm taking more from him in the future. Would highly recommend.

I loved Dr. Sperling's class, and there was probably no better time to take it. He not only taught us about the history of the relationship in an engaging way, but also allowed for open discussion at the beginning of class to talk about current events! Great lecturer and teacher.

Dr. Sperling is a great lecturer! He makes it really easy to understand the content and makes the requirements and expectations on exam and projects very clear. The only thing I didn't like about this course was the group project, but that was such a small part of the course that it didn't really matter. Definitely take him if you can!!!!

Professor Sriram is a great professor for a class like Math Stat. Exams are graded generously and attendance is optional, but there are random in class activities. Take his class if you can.
He's awesome. Super helpful and he grades very nicely.

If you are taking any statistics classes, try to get one that is taught by Dr. Sriram. He explains things better than almost anyone in the department and is so knowledgable. Professor Spooner is an awesome teacher. He is a very engaging lecturer and you can tell he really enjoys teaching. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is important to go as his tests are drawn from his lectures and he doesn't post much on ELC. Overall, would definitely take.

100 % recommend her for any class . She was one of the best professors i have had and this class is not even in my major . Lectures and content keep you engaged . Dr. Saint is the coolest professor Ive ever had at UGA. She is so kind and understanding, has the coolest thoughts and opinions, and the material for this class taught me more about relevant life lessons than any other class Ive had. If you get the chance to take her please please do.

Dr. Sui is a great professor. He is very understanding and his grading is lenient, giving credit on exams for effort. People said they didn't learn a lot in this class and that it was easy, but I disagree. I learned a lot and Dr. Sui is such a nice man and super good at explaining things at office hours. He doesn't treat you different for asking questions you should know. LONG LIVE CHINA.
